-Bulls Runner (+200%) and Identity MD (+150%) led top movers

It's been 5 weeks since we learned about the OpenAI/Hugging Face breach, which revealed an awkward reality: defenders have to ask models the same questions attackers do.

In this conversation, Cotool CEO Max Pollard and Neo CEO Nick Warner sit down with a16z's Joel de la Garza at Black Hat to discuss how security tools were designed to stop people or malware (and how AI agents are neither), what breaks when half of enterprise software goes agentic, and how teams are routing around cyber refusals.

00:00 Intro
01:00 Models escaping containment & the Hugging Face breach
01:50 Why models refuse to help the good guys
05:45 Built to stop people and malware, but agents are neither
06:45 "The end justifies the means, in the mind of the model"
10:45 50% of enterprise apps agentic before 2027
14:20 When your honeypot becomes a false positive machine
15:25 Signatures are dead, and so is behavioral detection
18:55 Defending AI and defending from AI

@maxpollard415 @cotoolai @neo_ai_security

tweets.text:
Hidden AI-related commitments are skyrocketing among Big Tech companies:

The top 9 US tech firms have ~$3 trillion in off-balance-sheet commitments, including leases for data centers and power infrastructure that have not yet commenced, as well as purchase commitments for AI-related equipment and services.

This is roughly triple the amount that these firms report on their balance sheets in leases and long-term debt.

This also compares to ~$600 billion in CapEx reported over the last year.

Alphabet, $GOOGL, alone posted an increase of more than +800% YoY in off-balance-sheet obligations, more than 7 times its YoY increase in CapEx.

This was followed by Meta, $META, which reported an increase of more than +750% YoY in such obligations, more than 9 times the increase in CapEx over the same period.

AI infrastructure is driving one of the largest corporate investment waves in history.

Term premium is back and structural. The Fed can cut the front end. The long end answers to buyers who demand to be paid. $TLT

Term premium is back and structural. The Fed can cut the front end. The long end answers to buyers who demand to be paid. $TLT

Sorry mate, I believe you're incorrect here.

Not only is the share count heavily diluted, but the proportion of the BTC 'assigned' to MSTR has decreased significantly since the prefs are now senior to the common.

As BTC price falls, the fixed fiat face value of the prefs (and debt) captures more of the balance sheet, and MSTR residual equity is literally worth less.

This is also now how the firm now calculates mNAV, so the mechanism here isn't hand waving.

Have done quite a bit of work to satisfy myself this is the case. Most of it indicated that June+ was going to be a rough period for MSTR, and it was.

Market suggested I was right in my thinking.
